title: Performance surgery checklist and on-call triage
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, action-oriented checklist and lightweight tooling reference for the on-call engineer or "runtime surgeon" who needs to quickly understand, capture, and stabilize serving-runtime performance regressions. It is intentionally terse — intended to be pasted into an incident Slack thread and followed step-by-step.

When to use:
- End-user throughput or p50/p95 latency degrades and customer requests increase a lot.
- Tail latency spikes isolated to a region/pool.
- Memory growth leading to OOMs on inference workers.
- High token cost vs baseline for a stable model (investigate batching / kv cache).

Quick triage timeline (0-5m):
1) Confirm scope: ask for request IDs, model, region, route, hostnames, and a short example input.
2) Check the console route dashboard + recent deploys. Screenshot dashboard (latency by route, error rate).
3) Identify a live host with elevated p95:
   - production logs: grep for high-latency request ids or search by route.
   - metrics: filter by host / container id.
4) If problem is systemic, notify SRE and product on-call. If single host, proceed.

Capture (5-20m): minimal-overhead captures to avoid perturbing production
- Always annotate captures with incident id and uploader. Naming: inc-<JIRA>-<host>-<YYYYMMDD>-<type>.
- Live sampling (low-overhead stack snapshots):
  - pstack-style (linux): sudo perf record -F 49 -g -p <PID> -o /tmp/trace.data -- sleep 10
  - convert to folded stacks: perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > /tmp/folded.stacks
  - render: ./flamegraph.pl /tmp/folded.stacks > /tmp/trace.svg
- eBPF micro-sample (short, safe):
  - bpftrace -e 'profile:hz:97 /pid == PID/ { @[ustack()] = count(); }' -d 10 > /tmp/bpftrace.out  # low overhead
- KV-cache hit ratio snapshot (app-level):
  - curl -s "http://localhost:9090/metrics|grep kvcache" or hit internal admin endpoints.
- Memory/GC snapshot: jmap/jcmd or heap dump depending on runtime. Dump to network share (not /tmp) if size > 50MB.

Lightweight helper scripts (paste into incident thread):
- quick-kvtrace.sh (example):
  #!/bin/bash
  PID=$1
  ts=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
  out=/tmp/inc-${INC_ID:-unknown}-$HOSTNAME-$ts-kvtrace.txt
  echo "capturing stacks for $PID -> $out"
  sudo perf record -F 49 -g -p $PID -o ${out}.data -- sleep ${2:-8} && sudo perf script -i ${out}.data > ${out}.folded && /opt/tools/flamegraph/flamegraph.pl ${out}.folded > ${out}.svg
  echo "uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/$out.svg"

- snapshot-to-s3 (curl + awscli minimal):
  aws s3 cp /tmp/inc-* s3://redwood-incidents/${INC_ID:-unknown}/ --acl private --storage-class STANDARD_IA

What to collect by symptom:
- High CPU / long syscalls: perf record + perf script, top -H, strace -f -p PID (5s).
- GC pauses: jstack/jcmd/gcore and GC logs (rotate).
- Tokenization/encoder hotpath: run a traced request on a canary host with profile flags enabled (see linked PR).
- GPU stalls / cuda syncs: nvidia-smi dmon and + capture process-level GPU metrics (nvprof only on repro).

Non-blocking capture guidance:
- Keep sampling windows short (5-15s) unless you have reason to run longer.
- Prefer user-space call graphs (dwarf) if available; avoid kernel-heavy trace unless investigating syscalls.
- Note: on quantized runs we may see a lot of kernel work — annotate whether quantized kernel mode was used.

Interpreting a quick flame snapshot (what to look for in the top frames):
- Very large single frame at top that is not in model code => blocking I/O or serialization issue.
- Many small frames in memcopy/alloc => excessive copies or fragmentation.
- GPU-sync / cudaMemcpy appearing in CPU stacks => sync on CPU side, may indicate missing async handling.
- Lock contention: repeated runtime_lock frames aggregated to p95/p99.

Stabilize (20-90m):
- If build/deploy is implicated, rollback to last good commit and re-run profled request to validate.
- Add temporary autoscale/burst for Dedicated pools if throughput-related and safe.
- If KV-cache miss rate increased: temporarily increase prefix caching TTL or promote a cache warm path for frequent keys.
- If batching misconfiguration: adjust max_batch_latency and max_batch_tokens in route config and test on canary.

Post-incident checklist (for the incident owner):
- Upload all captures to s3://redwood-incidents/<INC>/ with a README describing host, PID, model, route, sample request.
- Create a perf ticket with reproducer steps and attach flame svgs and folded stacks. Link to JIRA-REINF-1983.
- If correlated to a PR, add a short regression test (microbenchmark) that asserts p95 <= baseline on stable workloads.
- Add a short note to the route dashboard explaining mitigation and postmortem link.

Quick reproducible benchmark recipe (dev):
- small local harness: python bench/mini_client.py --model foo --seq 512 --batch 1 --n 1000 --concurrency 8 --trace=perf && python tools/stack_to_svg.py out.folded -o out.svg
- For consistent CI: run against a pinned VM image, pin driver/kernel if GPU measurements are required. Document exact AMI/container digest in the job.

Incident annotations and metadata conventions (so we can search later):
- Incident ID: INC-<JIRAKEY>-<YYYYMMDD> (e.g. INC-REINF-1983-20260214)
- Tags: region:<region>, pool:<pool-name>, model:<model-name>, symptom:<latency|oom|gpu|mem-leak>
- Artifacts: s3 path to traces (stackfolded, svg), job ids, container image digest, kernel version.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Add a low-noise, always-on periodic lightweight stack sampler per node (enable opt-in flags for Dedicated customers).
- Improve script to automatically annotate flamegraph frames with package names using our build-id map.
- Provide a canary-mode which runs a single traced request under controlled latency overhead for deterministic repro.

Notes / references:
- Minimal perf workflow borrowed from infra/ops (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/742).
- Benchmark baseline table is in Confluence: Perf Bench Results.
- Example incident with full captures: JIRA-REINF-1420 (search internal).

If you're oncall and stuck: ping @eng-sre and add the short capture artifacts link into the page. Keep captures private to the incident S3 bucket until triage is complete.

Authors: Aisha Khan (lead), Jon Ortega, Li Wei.
